financial_property_loss: Wrongful loss to the complainant's company by robbing its due chance to get a contract for the Boiler Plant Units at Korba
premeditation_planning: The court found that the allegations of fabricating the records were mischievously made as an afterthought just to give colour of criminality to a civil case
motive: To convert a case with civil nature into criminal prosecution
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the tender rejection was in furtherance of and in discharge of the official duties by the appellant, including reports from JSEB officials and technical experts indicating the respondent's unsatisfactory performance.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the reports from JSEB officials and technical experts were against the respondent and supported the tender rejection.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: Not stated; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: Not stated
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Rahul Srivastava, Ram Swarup Sharma; Counsel for the State: Not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated; High Court: Dismissed the petition of the appellants; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order and dismissed the complaint
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants, being public servants, could not be prosecuted without prior sanction from the competent authority under Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. They also contended that the respondent's allegations were a misuse and abuse of the process of law, as the complaint was filed after exhausting civil remedies.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the allegations made by the respondent were fabricated and made as an afterthought to convert a civil case into a criminal prosecution. They also contended that the actions of the appellants were in furtherance of their official duties and that the respondent had no locus standi to file the complaint.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that if an offence is alleged to have been committed by a public servant while acting in discharge of official duties, prior sanction under Section 197 is required. The Court also applied the test from Dr. Budhikota Subbarao that if the act has a reasonable connection with the discharge of duty, Section 197 applies.
precedent_relied_upon: Shambhoo Nath Misra v. State of U.P. (1997) 5 SCC 326; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Indian Oil Corpn. v. NEPC India Ltd. (2006) 6 SCC 736; lnder Mohan Goswami and another v. State of Uttaranchal and Ors. (2007) 12 SCC 1
